transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
In Michigan, the race for U.S. Senate has taken a new twist
as a former Democratic primary hopeful now says she's endorsing the Republican candidate.
The news comes two days before the midterm elections.
NPR's Ava Berger reports.
Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens broke with her party Sunday.
She posted on her social media that she was endorsing Michigan's Republican candidate,
Mike Rogers, over fellow Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.
I don't belong in Abdul's campaign.
Stevens also endorsed Rogers outside of a church event
and said she still is a Democrat but didn't feel welcome in El-Sayed's campaign.
This split comes after El-Sayed told reporters he didn't want Stevens to attend
a different church service Sunday with him.
That was meant to show unity among Democrats.
In August, El-Sayed beat Stevens in a bitter primary
in which the pair clashed over U.S. support for Israel.
Initially, Stevens had endorsed El-Sayed in the race.
Ava Berger, NPR News, Washington.
Immigration advocates in the Sacramento region say
federal agents are carrying out increasingly aggressive operations there.
That's raising concerns as Election Day approaches.
CAP Radio's Gerardo Zavala has our reports.
Giselle Garcia with Immigrant Rights Group NorCal Resist
says an observer saw federal agents smash a car window
and drag a man out of the vehicle.
In another incident caught on video, Garcia says agents
forcibly removed a man from a restaurant.
This might very well be just the new normal.
UC Davis Law Professor Kevin Johnson says he thinks the timing is significant.
It's not a coincidence that Election Day is coming.
NPR reached out to the Department of Homeland Security for comment,
but they did not respond.
For NPR News, I'm Gerardo Zavala in Sacramento.
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Truesk vows to continue his overhaul
of the Constitutional Court that despite protests about the suspension
of the Chief Justice installed by the previous administration.
As Esme Nicholson reports, it's just the latest
in a decade-long political stalemate over the judiciary.
In a speech to the nation, the centrist and pro-EU
Prime Minister Truesk said the shake-up was vital
if Poland is to restore conditions for independent justice and rule of law.
His address follows efforts by some government-backed judges
to seize control of the court and suspend the court's Chief Justice
and Deputy, both of whom were appointed by the opposition party.
Truesk described the tribunal, reformed by the previous administration,
as not a genuine court.
He criticized Poland's President Karol Navroski for forcing his way
into the court building on Friday night.
Navroski accuses Truesk of a forcible takeover of a constitutional body.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
And you're listening to NPR News.
One person was killed and a number of others are listed in critical condition
after a college football game Saturday night near Legion Field
in Birmingham, Alabama.
The Gulf States newsroom's Joseph King has an update.
Nine people were shot shortly after the Magic City Classic,
an annual football game between two in-state historically black colleges,
Alabama A&M and Alabama State.
Officials say the victims are between 19 to 30 years old.
A 17-year-old in custody was found in possession of a Glock switch,
an illegal attachment that converts a handgun into an automatic weapon.
Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin says the shooting does not represent
the football game's 85-year history in the city.
We will continue to support, defend and uplift our city's historically black traditions.
Officials say multiple guns will recover at the scene
and believe there are other shooters at large.
The Magic City Classic draws in hundreds of thousands of visitors
and generates over $20 million.
For NPR News, I'm Joseph King in Birmingham.
There was also a shooting in Dallas Saturday that left four people dead
and 15 others injured across three shooting locations.
Having Halloween on a weekend may be good for candy sales,
but it was tough on movie theaters.
Studio estimates suggest total earnings across North America
were no more than $56 million, making it the second slowest of the year.
The documentary "You Can See Everything" landed in first place
with $10.6 million in ticket sales.
The horror flick "Clayface" was in second, trailing by $200,000.
And the animated film "Wildwood" claimed third place with $7.5 million in sales.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Rep. Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
Immigration advocates in Sacramento report increasingly aggressive federal agent operations ahead of Election Day
Polish PM Donald Tusk vows to continue overhaul of Constitutional Court despite protests
One killed, nine shot after Magic City Classic football game near Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama
Dallas shootings leave four dead and 15 injured across three locations
Halloween weekend box office is second slowest of the year; documentary 'You Can See Everything' tops chart
